mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) signals accommodative monetary policy that reduces equity discount rates, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS remains below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 9.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of months when UNRATE exceeds 9.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a sharp contraction in consumer demand, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases (Rank IC < 0.02).

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100) signals supply chain disruptions that increase inflation expectations, causing S&P 500 underperformance over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO is below 100.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained non-farm payrolls growth (PAYEMS > 100,000) indicates a strengthening labor market that supports consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of months when PAYEMS growth exceeds 100,000.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) falling below 650,000 units signals a weakening housing market that reduces consumer confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of months when HOUST is below 650.0.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous federal funds rate increases (FEDFUNDS rise) and core inflation declines (CPIAUCSL fall) signal ineffective monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising FEDFUNDS and falling CPIAUCSL fails to predict negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases (Rank IC < 0.02).

mechanism_narrative: Declining real GDP growth (GDPC1 growth rate < 0.5% annualized) signals economic slowdown that reduces corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 growth rate is below 0.5%.
